project_profile.project_description: This project develops supervised machine learning models to predict residential property prices using historical housing market data. The project is currently in development and is intended for internal analytical use. The system produces numeric price predictions rather than free-text output.

extraction_metadata.document_summary: The Housing Price Prediction Model project is in the development stage, using supervised machine learning to predict residential property prices. It is managed by Eljo Example, with Jordan Lee as the primary contact, and reviewed by Moe Example within the Economic Analysis Division. The project uses internal historical housing market data, some of which contains personal information, but no sensitive or confidential data, nor third-party data. It trains models from scratch using open-source Python libraries and does not use generative AI, LLMs, AI agents, information retrieval, fine-tuning, third-party models, external pretrained models, or foundation models. The system produces numeric price predictions and is planned for internal operational deployment, requiring human oversight. It supports analytical decisions but does not interact with external end-users. The team is reviewing whether model outputs could be linked to identifiable personal information.
